title: Civilian monitors will investigate Indigenous man's death in B.C. police cells
subtitle: Surrance Myers, 21, died after going into medical distress in police custody in Williams Lake on Oct. 1, 2022
article: The director of the Independent Investigations Office of B.C. has called in civilian monitors to look into the 2022 death of a Williams Lake man in police cells.

The appointed monitors were selected by the Tŝilhqot'in First Nation and will have "unfettered access to all investigative materials, including all evidence and statements collected, and the IIO's investigative team will provide any assistance requested," said chief civilian director Ronald J. MacDonald in a statement.
The investigation was opened shortly after a First Nations man went into medical distress while in police custody and died on Oct. 1, 2022.
The man, identified by family as Surrance Myers, 21, was picked up the night before while he and a woman were riding a moped.
Williams Lake RCMP did not say at the time why he had been arrested, and there were calls for police to be more accountable and culturally sensitive from the First Nations community.

"I thank the leadership of the Tŝilhqot'in National Government for working in partnership with my office to appoint these monitors," said MacDonald. "I have said it before: the IIO is committed to earning the trust of Indigenous Peoples and building confidence in police accountability."

"The IIO continues to work diligently to recruit an even more diverse workforce to ensure we are representative of the people we serve. In the interim, I look forward to receiving the monitor's reports and commit to undertaking any additional considerations, evidence, or other avenues of investigation they identify."
The monitors' report will be made public on the IIO website, the normal process after its investigations into police actions or inactions that led to injury or death.
